title: Whiteboard jam — eviction scorer & warmup playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a succinct capture of a whiteboard jam (informal) where we sketched an eviction scoring model and a pragmatic warmup playbook for mixed-length sessions. Goal: arrive at a prioritized list of follow-ups and an experiment plan we can sprint on next cycle.

Date/Time: 2025-11-05 11:00–12:10 PT
Attendees: Priya, Evan, Diego, Sandra, Marta, Alexei
Context: ongoing complaints about poor p99 for short interactive queries when KV-cache churn is high; Dedicated customers seeing spikes after bursty multi-turn flows. Related to RI-987 and recent hot/cold cache hierarchy notes.

Quick summary of problem statements we agreed on:
- Current eviction is mostly LRU-ish with tenant-weighted adjustments; it ignores short-term warming signals and cross-session usefulness of prefixes.
- Warmup (model KV prefetching) exists but is brittle: cold-start for many small sessions still pays latency penalty. Warmup also increases bursty GPU memory for low-value prefixes.
- Need low-risk changes that preserve throughput and avoid cascading OOMs on Dedicated pools.

Brainstormed scoring signals for eviction (ranked by perceived signal quality):
1) recent-ttl-decay: time-decayed recency score (exponential) — easy to compute, low overhead.
2) convo-reuse-frequency: how often a prefix is referenced across sessions in last N minutes — higher reuse -> lower eviction priority.
3) completion-cost: estimated token-generation cost if prefix must be recomputed; rough proxy: avg tokens-used following prefix historically.
4) model-variant-compat: whether cached tensor layout is compatible across quantization or variant fallbacks (incompatible => higher eviction).
5) error-sensitivity: observed downstream quality drop when prefix missing (from eval hits) — expensive to maintain but valuable for customer-facing flows.
6) p99-tail-contribution: measured impact on tail latency when cached vs cold; useful to protect prefixes that avoid high tail.

Proposed combined eviction score (sketch, not final math):
- base_score = alpha * ttl_decay + beta * reuse_frequency - gamma * completion_cost + delta * compatibility_bonus - epsilon * tail_sensitivity
- We should keep coefficients simple and monotonic; avoid heavy ML at first. Aim for linear combination with integerized buckets for fast comparison.

Warmup playbook: when to proactively warm KV for an incoming session
- On-session-arrival heuristics (cheap):
  - customer-tier == enterprise && last-request-within-5m: aggressive warm (prefetch top-K prefixes used by that customer in last 24h).
  - short-interactive-sessions prediction (model on request metadata): warm top-1 prefix (only if reuse_frequency > threshold).
- Conditional warm strategies:
  - budgeted warm: attach a per-tenant warm_credit counter replenished slowly; only spend if warm_credit > 0 to avoid bursts.
  - probabalistic warm: sample a fraction p of sessions to warm to measure impact; ramp p up for customers that see benefit.
- Warm scope: prefer warming compact KV slices (attention-key/value heads for first N layers) rather than full-state for large models. This reduces memory pressure.

Operational constraints we must respect:
- Warm operations should be cancellable when node memory pressure crosses a soft threshold (drain mechanism).
- Prefetch priority must be deprioritized behind live inference; no warm should preempt in-flight tokens.
- Add observability: metric for warm success (latency delta when warm vs cold), warm-induced OOMs, and warm memory footprint.

Decisions reached (consensus):
1) Implement a staged eviction_score that combines ttl_decay + reuse_frequency + completion_cost proxy. Keep compatibility/quality signals as optional flags for canary. (Owner: Evan)
2) Implement a budgeted warm_credit mechanism at tenant level; start with conservative defaults. (Owner: Diego)
3) Warm scope will initially be "compact-kv-first" — implement a layer-limited prefetch API. (Owner: Sandra)
4) Defer fancy ML-based scoring/learning-to-rank until we have 4–6 weeks of warm metrics. Keep MR small. (Owner: Priya)

Action items and near-term experiments (priority order):
- A1: Evan -> prototype eviction_score module (in rust runtime) that exports top-N eviction candidates and a per-cache debug endpoint. Target spike PR in 1 week.
- A2: Diego -> implement warm_credit bookkeeping in slot-manager and add warm admission check. Target experimental rollout to 10% of traffic in 2 weeks.
- A3: Sandra -> implement compact-kv prefetch API + minimal kernel path to materialize partial KV. Target internal test harness by EOW.
- A4: Marta -> synthetic workload: create a mixed-length session generator that mimics SaaS chat (short bursts + occasional long convo) and runs in perf infra. Needed for tuning coefficients.
- A5: Priya -> add observability dashboards: warm_success_rate, warm_memory_bytes, eviction_score_histogram, tail_delta_by_warm. PR linked to GH: r-infer/issue/1234.

Experiment design notes:
- Rollout plan: canary on non-critical tenant pool -> measure p50/p95/p99 for short queries, and monitor memory pressure.
- Success criteria: p99 reduction >= 5% for short interactive flows with <2% increase in memory footprint per-node and zero warm-induced OOMs during canary.
- Fallback: if memory pressure crosses 80% during canary, auto-disable warm_credit spending for the affected node pool.

Open questions / unresolved risks:
- How to compute completion-cost reliably without expensive logging? (suggestion: approximate from tokens-per-response by prompt hash; privacy note: only aggregate counts)
- Cross-tenant reuse fairness: protecting cross-tenant reused prefixes could favor noisy tenants. Need per-tenant weighting guardrails.
- Interaction with multi-variant routing: warmed KV might be incompatible if request falls back to a smaller quantized variant. Need quick compatibility checks before warm.

Next sync: quick follow-up on 2025-11-12 to review Evan's prototype and Sandra's prefetch API. If prototype looks good, schedule a 2-week canary.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep math simple. Buckets instead of floats. Avoid global sorts on every eviction pass — use per-slab candidate lists and lazy re-score.
- Document warm_credit semantics clearly for Dedicated customers (they will want control).
- Link the final scoring formula and config knobs in the runtime config page in Confluence.

Appendix: rough pseudocode for budgeted warm credit check (sketch)
- on_session_start(tenant):
    if tenant.warm_credit <= 0: return skip_warm
    if sample_random() > tenant.warm_prob: return skip_warm
    schedule_prefetch(compact_kv_topK)
    tenant.warm_credit -= cost_of_compact_kv(compact_kv_topK)

End of notes.
